title: 3am runbook embroidery — kernel triage & perf TODOs
content:
Context and quick goals:
- Late-night thread: p99 burst on model-v3 between 02:00–02:45 UTC. Sparse but consistent across 3 hosts (gpu-pool-b).
- Goal: capture small reproducible case, rapid mitigations to reduce impact tomorrow morning, postmortem seed notes.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) KV cache thrash: eviction hotspot when many short context requests mix with long streaming sessions. suspect: eviction due to per-worker cache size rounding on quantized model.
2) CUDA driver/gpu-power throttling correlated with NVML warnings in logs (see slack thread).
3) Scheduler contention: metronome -> batching boundary misalignment causing tiny batches at high qps (costly warmups).
4) Client-induced tail events (bad prompt storm from a single key) — filtered but need sample.

What I did at 03:10–03:40 (commands / observations):
- pulled syslogs: grep nvml /var/log/runtime/* -> repeating WARN: nvml GPU ECC event (host 03/10 02:12) on host-17.
- ran quick profile on host-17 with perf counter snapshot (cpu cycles and context switches): small spike aligned with the nvml messages.
- collected a microtrace of a p99 request (trace id attached in slack). saw 40ms stall in kernel->cuda interaction.

Quick mitigations to test (order & owner):
- [ ] increase per-worker kv-cache soft limit from 1.2GB -> 1.6GB on a canary host (Priya). Should reduce evictions. (JIRA-RT-8242)
- [ ] adjust metronome tick to align batch windows (add 6ms offset for gpu-pool-b) — run A/B for 1 hour (Aman/Diego).
- [ ] temporarily throttle incoming QPS for the noisy API key (rate-limit to 3rps) to see if tail dissolves (Product Ops owns key gating).
- [ ] engage infra to check node thermal/power telemetry for host-17 and host-19 overnight — ask SRE to keep NVML logging verbose for 24h (Diego).

Experiments to capture reproducible case:
- Re-run the p99 trace with NVTX annotations enabled across the whole pipeline. Use model-v3, sequence length 1024, interleaving 1:3 short:long. Compare with pristine host. (script: /scripts/trace_kv_run.sh -i 100 -s 1024)
- Synthetic client to replay the observed request mix at 50% QPS to avoid full outage but still trigger tail. Run on canary network namespace to isolate.

Data to collect (attach to postmortem):
- nvml logs and dmesg for 02:00–03:00 UTC from host-16..20 (SRE export tarball).
- runtime trace ids for 20 p99 events (I saved 5 locally: t-abc123, t-def456...). Need export.
- batch scheduler metrics (metronome offsets, batch size histogram) for pool-b for the hour window.

Pending TODOs and notes to self:
- [ ] Convert kernel observation into small repro that fails in CI (create unit test to simulate eviction pattern). Owner: Aman, due EOD next Tuesday.
- [ ] Draft short ops note for morning cooldown: 4 bullet mitigations + who to loop in (SRE, Product, Solutions). Keep under 6 sentences. (Priya)
- [ ] Check PR #1198 for recent changes to kv-cache rounding logic (possible regression) — add comment to author to run heavy tail bench. (Aman)
- [ ] Follow up on GPU power events with infra after 09:30 PT standup (Diego).

Open questions / TODO research bits:
- How often does eviction rounding happen vs actual memory pressure? Need histogram of per-worker commitment. (metric: serving.kv.cache.per_worker_bytes)
- Does quantized memory layout increase frag/alloc patterns that look like pressure? Ask research: Amir?
- If we bump per-worker cache, what's expected P95 token latency delta under small-batch workloads? Run bench soon.

Notes for the morning incident call (bullet script):
- quick TL;DR: transient p99 burst likely caused by kv-cache eviction + small scheduler misalignment; low severity but visible for some customers between 02:00–02:45 UTC.
- actions taken: increased logging, collecting nvml traces, running canary kv-cache bump, scheduling A/B metronome test.
- immediate ask: SRE to verify power/thermal logs; Product to hold noisy key if tail persists; Disable quantization fallback on model-v3 canary if suspicious.

Small housekeeping / mental notes:
- keep this file concise. Move to a proper postmortem doc if we confirm cross-host impact.
- remember to cite github PR and Jira. Add links in final doc.

Scratch snippets (commands to re-run quickly):
- collect dmesg: sudo journalctl -k --since "2026-03-10 01:50" --until "2026-03-10 03:10" > /tmp/dmesg-host17.txt
- nvml dump: python /opt/runtime/tools/nvml_dump.py --since 2026-03-10T02:00 --host host-17 > /tmp/nvml-host17.json
- run trace harness: /scripts/trace_kv_run.sh -i 100 -s 1024 -o /tmp/trace-out.json

Random thought to vet: if metronome shift reduces tiny batches but increases latency variance in mid-percentiles, is that an acceptable trade for customers on Dedicated? Need policy decision. Flag for product review.

End of late-night embroidery. Will tidy and push an ops note in the morning.
